proposals.evidence: DEDR 5160 directly groups the first-person singular forms in these languages. The source cognacy annotation explicitly identifies this article; full-article checking confirms the same pronoun family. Survey aēn and hēnu retain their differences from dictionary Kurukh ēn and Malto én; these are comparative proposals, not spelling corrections. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3647 directly groups Brahui nan, Kannada nāvu, Kurukh nām, Malto nám, Tamil nām and Telugu manamu as the inclusive/general first-person plural series. The survey cognacy annotation identifies this article. The survey gloss remains simply we; no inclusive label is inserted into source data. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
